next_step: Use both worker-units for a preregistered, matched holdout comparison on a prospective workload from the promised family. Measure acquisition and preparation plus execution cost for the learned scaffold and the strongest equally informed conventional method, allowing both to use the thin representation. Check output correctness on the same tasks.
allocation: One unit specifies the workload, cost boundary, and comparison protocol; one unit implements and runs the comparison.
decisive_observation: Whether the learned approach has lower end-to-end cost than the conventional incumbent while producing correct outputs on the holdout workload.
outcome_decisions: If it wins, continue testing amortized gains on additional tasks. If it ties or loses, stop prioritizing this scaffold and explore a different retained representation. If correctness fails, repair or reject the implementation before drawing cost conclusions.
retained_result: Keep the verified scale/Hessian agreement at seven declared replay points and the observed interpreter operation counts. They establish limited correctness and count comparisons, not speed or reusable learning gains.
uncertainty: The current representation is the weakest consequential link: it has not shown lower total cost, and the conventional incumbent may adopt the same thin representation. A negative result applies only to the tested family and workload; wall-time and broader generalization remain unknown.
